metadata.updatePolicy: Every shipped user-facing feature, support-content change, or bug fix gets an entry here. Test-only, CI-only, and internal refactors are not listed.

updates.title: Live Call Flow aligned to the new Ogletree Tier 1 standard
updates.changed: Replaced the older seven-stage call journey with the current Ogletree Tier 1 Zoom Support flow: Opening / Greeting → Active Listening & Acknowledgment → Empathy Statement → Assurance / Ownership → Caller & Hearing Identification → Probing / Diagnostic Questions → Troubleshooting → Confirmation of Resolution → Recap / Summary → Final Check → Closing. Navigator now captures Hearing Status and who is affected early in the call, shows the source’s simple Greet → Listen → Empathize → Assure → Probe → Troubleshoot → Confirm → Close formula, and displays the resolved versus unresolved branch after confirmation. Locate → Describe → Guide → Confirm remains the troubleshooting method inside Step 7 rather than the entire call flow. Training Roadmap, Call Language, Guided Visual Lessons, and Scenario Scripts were aligned to the new sequence.

updates.title: Guided Visual Lessons turn core support concepts into visual patterns
updates.changed: Added five short, source-backed Guided Visual Lessons inside Training & Resources: the official Ogletree call flow, device-first orientation, speaker-versus-microphone symptom direction, Waiting for host versus Waiting Room, and the basic-support stop/referral boundary. Each lesson uses a compact visual flow or side-by-side comparison, shows three call-ready takeaways, and links to the exact existing approved resource instead of duplicating the full workflow. The Training Roadmap now marks Guided Visual Lessons as available; Practice Lab remains reserved for Phase 6 Batch 3.

updates.changed: Added a visual Training Roadmap as the default home inside Training & Resources. Available modules open the exact existing resource without duplicating content, while unfinished Phase 6 modules are clearly marked as coming in later batches.

updates.title: Scope Check now completes the referral handoff
updates.changed: Extended Scope Check with the approved referral / roadblock matrix. When a case reaches Stop + Refer, agents now choose the exact roadblock and the workspace identifies who owns the next step, shows the agent boundary, provides source-backed handoff wording, and lets the agent copy that wording. The tool covers Waiting Room admission, host-controlled permissions, incorrect meeting details, unresolved joining issues, account/admin access, device-level hardware detection, organization-managed permissions, network/security restrictions, possible Zoom product issues after basic troubleshooting, proceeding decisions, and privacy/recording/confidentiality/AI-policy questions. the workspace does not invent a person, phone number, email address, or promise an internal escalation.

updates.title: Scope Check now tells agents when to continue or stop
updates.changed: Added a global Scope Check live tool beside Call Documentation. Agents can classify the remaining action, indicate how far approved troubleshooting has progressed, and confirm whether the next step stays within approved authority. the workspace then returns Continue Approved Troubleshooting, Stop + Refer, Resolved — Document & Close, or More Information Needed. The decision path follows the approved Zoom Basic Support Boundaries resource and does not invent referral contacts or promise internal escalation. The Navigator resolution status was also renamed from Escalation Needed to Referral Needed to match the approved handoff model.

updates.title: What’s New now follows a clear release-entry rule
updates.changed: Defined the What’s New page as the user-facing release log for the workspace. Every shipped user-facing feature, support-content change, or bug fix must receive an update entry. Test-only changes, CI maintenance, and invisible internal refactors stay out of the user-facing log so the page remains useful instead of becoming raw commit history.

updates.title: Common Issue Routes added to Navigator
updates.changed: Added the first Phase 2 live-call routing layer for five high-frequency concerns: Can’t join the meeting, I can’t hear anyone, They can’t hear me, My camera isn’t working, and I’m waiting to get in. Each route starts from the caller’s symptom, asks only the questions that change the path, separates symptoms from assumed causes, shows one-step-at-a-time guidance and expected results, keeps Waiting for host distinct from Waiting Room, carries forward the Phase 1 device/role/status context, and preserves access to approved Process Documents plus traceable official Zoom Support sources. Natural caller-language search now surfaces these fast routes before deeper process results when appropriate.

updates.title: Original Phase 1 Core Live Call Flow (superseded Sep 19)
updates.changed: Added the Phase 1 live-call foundation at the top of Navigator: Opening → Acknowledgment → Identify → Resolution → Recap → Adjacent Issues → Closing. The flow uses Step / Agent Action / Suggested Script columns, includes device selection for Windows, Mac, iPhone, Android, and Browser, identifies Host vs Participant, and records Resolved / Unresolved / Escalation Needed status. The previous four-step workflow banner was removed so agents see one clear call journey. Existing search and process tools remain available below the flow. This original seven-stage flow was superseded on September 19 by the new Ogletree Tier 1 standard call flow; see the newer Call Flow Alignment entry for the current workflow.

updates.title: Strict QA findings remediated
updates.changed: Resolved the strict QA findings that affected live-call usability and accessibility. Closed mobile navigation is no longer keyboard-focusable, natural caller-language search now routes key support phrases more reliably, long Call Guides use progressive disclosure without removing approved content, avatar selection and process tabs have efficient keyboard behavior, form errors identify their fields, dialogs prevent background scrolling, and the active navigation item is announced to assistive technology. Supabase hardening also removed unintended client execution of an internal SECURITY DEFINER helper, moved citext out of the exposed public schema, optimized RLS auth checks, and added missing foreign-key indexes.

updates.title: Privacy-safe usage, presence, and feedback administration
updates.changed: Connected the existing analytics tables to the Support Workspace. Authenticated sessions now heartbeat roughly once per minute, active time stops after five minutes without interaction, stale presence is treated as offline, Usage Analytics includes zero-usage users with Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Custom views, and the Feedback Queue now supports audited status changes plus Open Page routing. Production CI also moved to Node 24 for compatibility with the current Supabase packages.
